objective: Proof: if a finite group G has an abelian normal subgroup N with G/N nilpotent (in particular every metabelian group), then for a finitely presented group whose first homology with coefficients in F_p has bounded dimension for every prime p dividing |G/N| (closed 3-manifolds with bounded |H1|, knot groups with meridians sent to a fixed class), the number of homomorphisms into G is computable in polynomial time: the maps into G/N are boundedly many and enumerable level by level, and the lifts of each form an affine space over the twisted 1-cocycles, counted by linear algebra; contrast with S4, whose maps into S3 can be exponentially many with H1 = Z. Standard-library check against brute force on random presentations.
status: Proved by BOUNDED-H1-20261025-001B-P001: if a finite group has an abelian normal subgroup N with nilpotent quotient Q (every metabelian group), counting homomorphisms from a finitely presented group with bounded mod-p first homology (p dividing |Q|), optionally with one generator sent into a fixed class, is polynomial: at most |Q|^d maps to Q, enumerated by F_p lifting, and the lifts through N counted by linear algebra over N; this covers closed 3-manifolds with bounded |H1| and knot groups with a meridian class, and contrasts with S4, which has no such decomposition and is #P-hard on knots (BOUNDED-H1-20261025-001A).
title: Metabelian targets stay polynomial with bounded homology
